claims.text: The material is an equimolar WTaTiVZr high-entropy alloy.
The WTaTiVZr alloy has a fine-grained, homogeneous microstructure.
Commercially processed pure tungsten is typically coarse-grained and highly brittle at room temperature.
WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
WTaTiVZr has greater toughness than pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
Atomic-scale lattice distortion and grain-boundary chemistry primarily control the proposed enhancement in plastic strain and toughness.
Adding Ta, Ti, V, and Zr to tungsten produces significant lattice distortion.
The alloy-induced lattice distortion reduces the effective Peierls barrier or dislocation-nucleation barrier.
The reduced barrier promotes more homogeneous dislocation glide and planar slip at high temperature.
Ti, V, and Zr preferentially segregate to WTaTiVZr grain boundaries.
Solute segregation increases grain-boundary cohesion and delays crack initiation and propagation.
The combined dislocation and grain-boundary effects enhance ductility and toughness relative to pure tungsten.
At temperatures of at least 1000 K, WTaTiVZr will show greater plastic strain before failure than pure tungsten.
At temperatures of at least 1000 K, WTaTiVZr will show greater fracture toughness and delayed crack initiation and propagation relative to pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit more active and homogeneous dislocation movement than pure tungsten during high-temperature loading.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate under plasma-facing temperatures of at least 1000 K but may not dominate at lower temperatures or under static conditions.
Matched WTaTiVZr and pure-tungsten specimens should be tested under identical high-temperature, thermal-cycling, and irradiation conditions.
In situ electron microscopy and atom-probe tomography can be used to assess dislocation behavior and grain-boundary solute segregation.
Failure to observe improved plastic strain or toughness, or failure to observe the proposed dislocation and segregation signatures, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial comparison specifies a fine-grained WTaTiVZr alloy versus typically coarse-grained commercial tungsten, whereas the falsification design requires comparable grain sizes and microstructural states. These describe materially different comparisons, and the former would confound composition with grain size.
